ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is dark brown with distinct white crossbands and a white collar. A key feature is the flattened head and large, forward-facing eyes with vertical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Travancore Wolf Snake is best identified by the distinct, narrow white or yellowish crossbands that break into a reticulated pattern along the sides of its body.
ai.habitat: The Travancore Wolf Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found in leaf litter or rock crevices at elevations ranging from lowlands to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Travancore Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for geckos and skinks under the cover of darkness. When threatened, it often coils and vibrates its tail.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon travancoricus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–7 eggs. Breeding generally occurs during the monsoon season, between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Travancore wolf snake is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
